title: Autoscaler observer telemetry mismatch causing reserved-pool underprovision and customer failover
creator: Aisha Ortiz
description:
Summary: During a regional surge on 2026-03-09 a mismatch between the autoscaler 'observer' service and the allocator's headroom accounting caused premature scale-down signals and stale headroom metrics. This led to reserved-pool depletion for several mid-size tenants and automatic fallbacks to lower-capacity / cheaper model variants, resulting in elevated latency and customer escalations.

Behavior observed: observer emitted scale-down decisions based on a delayed headroom gauge (observer.headroom_seconds_stale > 30s) while allocator had already reclaimed slots. The observer's smoothing window incorrectly ignored 급성 bursts, driving the system to reduce proactive replenishment. The net effect: decreased burst budget, failed canary replenishes, and several tenants hit burst limits.

Why unique/different: This ticket focuses on the telemetry transformation layer in front of the autoscaler rather than allocator algorithm tuning. Root cause sits at the observer aggregation + TTL sampling logic rather than the scaling policy itself.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a canary cluster with autoscaler-2.4.0 and observer-service v1.11 with synthetic tenant workload generator (load pattern: sudden 6x RPS for 60s).
2) Instrument observer.headroom_gauge and allocator.available_slots metrics, enable debug logging for observer.sample-window=30s.
3) Trigger a surge from two simulated tenants with short-lived burst traffic and watch for observer emitting scale-downs within the first 90s despite allocator remaining under 70% utilization.
4) Verify that observer.headroom_seconds_stale > 30 and observer.smoothing_window dropped effective headroom by >40%.
timeline_comments: 2026-03-09 19:34 - PagerDuty: On-call alerted by elevated tenant errors; latency + errors spike correlated with reserved-pool RCU drops. - (oncall: Priya Nair)
2026-03-09 20:02 - First triage: Confirmed reserved-pool depletion pattern across two AZs; opened interim mitigation to increase pool buffer for affected tenants. - (Aisha Ortiz)

2026-03-10 09:15 - Engineering deep-dive: Observed mismatch between observer.view (Prometheus aggregation) and allocator internal counters (gRPC snapshot). Hypothesis: aggregation TTL / query window is truncating burst signals. - (Marcus Lee)

2026-03-11 14:40 - Hotfix deployed: Reverted observer sampling_window from 30s to 6s and added a fail-open when headroom_seconds_stale > 15s. Canary passed for 2 hours. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1598 - (Marcus Lee)

2026-03-12 08:20 - Customer comms: Notified top affected tenants with preliminary RCA and ETA for permanent fix. Logged at: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/DEDICATED-ESCALATION-555001 - (Customer Success: Elena Kim)

2026-03-13 11:05 - Observability work: Added two Grafana panels and an alert rule: observer_vs_allocator_headroom_mismatch_ratio > 0.15 for 3m. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/observer-allocator-headroom - (Observability: Rajesh Patel)
2026-03-15 10:30 - Running integration tests for new reconciliation logic; aim to submit full patch for review today. - (Marcus Lee)
investigation_findings: Observer sampling code uses Prometheus client side aggregation with a hard 30s window; during microbursts this averaged away headroom signals.
Allocator uses instantaneous counters with 5s TTL; mismatch between sampled average and instant counters caused inverted decisions.
Smoothing window reduction logic did not consider stale-data fail-open behaviour, so stale metrics suppressed proactive scale-ups.
Telemetry surfaced insufficiently: no explicit metric for 'stale_read_ratio' which would have made detection earlier.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Short-term: reduce observer sampling window and add stale-data fail-open to prevent suppressing scale-ups. Chosen because low-risk and rapid rollback path exists.

Mid-term: implement reconciliation loop that compares observer aggregated view with allocator instant counters and biases decisions toward allocator when mismatch persists >15s. This increases coupling but improves correctness for bursts.

Long-term: propose moving critical headroom signals to a strongly-consistent path (gRPC push from allocator to observer) to avoid aggregation artifacts. More engineering effort and risk; scheduled as follow-up.
resolution_summary: Temporary mitigation (observer sampling window rollback + stale-data fail-open) rolled out 2026-03-11 and restored normal reserved-pool headroom for affected tenants. Permanent reconciliation patch implementing observer<->allocator cross-check submitted as PR #1604; needs code review and an extended canary (48h under synthetic burst tests). Follow-ups: instrument stale_read_ratio, add customer-facing SLA telemetry per-tenant, and schedule architecture work to add push-based headroom sync (Q2 project).
next_steps: 1) Complete PR #1604 code review and merge; run 48h canary with synthetic burst profile (owner: Marcus Lee, due 2026-03-18).
2) Add stale_read_ratio metric to prometheus instrumentation (owner: Rajesh Patel, estimate 2 points).
3) Update dedicated capacity runbooks with new rollback and mitigation steps and notify SRE rotation (owner: Aisha Ortiz).
4) Kick off scoping doc for push-based headroom sync between allocator and observer (owner: Eng Arch - schedule in roadmap for Q2).
5) Postmortem write-up and customer-facing RCA to be published by 2026-03-20.
